vulnerabilities.title: Web Server Version Disclosure: Microsoft-IIS/8.5
vulnerabilities.description:
### 📍 Vulnerability Location
- **Target URL**: `http://testaspnet.vulnweb.com/`
- **Vulnerable Component / Parameter**: `HTTP Response Header: Server / X-Powered-By`
- **Protocol & Port**: `http` / Port 80

### 💥 Exploitation Proof & Payload
- **Tested Payload / Indicator**: `Banner String in HTTP Response: 'Web server version banner exposed: 'Microsoft-IIS/8.5'.'`
- **Verification Vector**: Automated Security Audit Probe
- **CVSS v3.1 Vector String**: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N`

### 🔬 Technical Analysis & Vulnerability Mechanics
Web server version banner exposed: 'Microsoft-IIS/8.5'.

### 📊 Threat Severity & CVSS v3.1 Scoring
- **CVSS v3.1 Unified Base Score**: **2.0 (Info)**
- **Authoritative Taxonomy**: **CWE-200**
- **Impact Assessment**: May permit unauthorized perimeter discovery, session integrity compromise, or execution alteration.
remediation_steps: Configure web server to suppress banner tokens.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Syntax Error Crash in 'id' Parameter
vulnerabilities.description:
### 📍 Vulnerability Location
- **Target URL**: `http://testaspnet.vulnweb.com/`
- **Vulnerable Component / Parameter**: `Network / Application Endpoint`
- **Protocol & Port**: `http` / Port 80

- **Tested Payload / Indicator**: `Automated scanner diagnostic signature verification`
- **Verification Vector**: Automated Security Audit Probe
- **CVSS v3.1 Vector String**: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

### 🔬 Technical Analysis & Vulnerability Mechanics
Injecting a single-quote syntax probe into parameter 'id' caused an unhandled backend database crash (response dropped from 13367 bytes to 0 bytes, status 200).
Tested URL: http://testaspnet.vulnweb.com/Comments.aspx?id=1%27

### 📊 Threat Severity & CVSS v3.1 Scoring
- **CVSS v3.1 Unified Base Score**: **9.5 (Critical)**
- **Authoritative Taxonomy**: **CWE-89**
- **Impact Assessment**: May permit unauthorized perimeter discovery, session integrity compromise, or execution alteration.
remediation_steps: Sanitize query parameters and bind inputs using prepared statements.

vulnerabilities.title: [AI-Hunter] Unhandled Database Crash (Potential Blind SQLi) in 'id'
vulnerabilities.description:
### 📍 Vulnerability Location
- **Target URL / Endpoint**: `/Comments.aspx`
- **Full Target URL**: `http://testaspnet.vulnweb.com/Comments.aspx?id=3%27`
- **Vulnerable Parameter / Component**: `id`
- **Service & Port**: `http` / Port 80

### 💥 Exploitation Proof & Payload
- **Tested Payload**: `'`
- **Verification Technique**: Severe response length anomaly (baseline > 800 bytes vs probe = 0 bytes)
- **CVSS v3.1 Vector**: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N`

### 🔬 Technical Analysis & Vulnerability Mechanics
Injecting single-quote syntax characters into parameter 'id' on /Comments.aspx caused the server to return an empty 0-byte response, whereas the baseline returned 14112 bytes. This severe crash differential strongly indicates an unhandled server-side database exception.

### 📊 Threat Severity & CVSS v3.1 Scoring
- **CVSS v3.1 Base Score**: **8.5 (High)**
- **Authoritative Classification**: **CWE-89**
- **Business Impact**: Unauthorized data compromise, application integrity degradation, or perimeter access bypass.
remediation_steps: Implement parameterized queries to safely bind user input.
Implement comprehensive error handling and logging without suppressing or abruptly terminating HTTP responses.

vulnerabilities.title: [AI-Hunter] Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) on 'id'
vulnerabilities.description:
### 📍 Vulnerability Location
- **Target URL / Endpoint**: `/Comments.aspx`
- **Full Target URL**: `http://testaspnet.vulnweb.com/Comments.aspx?id=4`
- **Vulnerable Parameter / Component**: `id`
- **Service & Port**: `http` / Port 80

### 💥 Exploitation Proof & Payload
- **Tested Payload**: `id=4`
- **Verification Technique**: Sequential identifier mutation successfully retrieved distinct record without authorization
- **CVSS v3.1 Vector**: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N`

### 🔬 Technical Analysis & Vulnerability Mechanics
Parameter 'id' on /Comments.aspx exposed distinct user/object records when incrementing value from 3 to 4 without session ownership validation.
Baseline URL: http://testaspnet.vulnweb.com/Comments.aspx?id=3
Mutated URL: http://testaspnet.vulnweb.com/Comments.aspx?id=4

### 📊 Threat Severity & CVSS v3.1 Scoring
- **CVSS v3.1 Base Score**: **8.5 (High)**
- **Authoritative Classification**: **CWE-639**
- **Business Impact**: Unauthorized data compromise, application integrity degradation, or perimeter access bypass.
remediation_steps: Implement server-side authorization checks verifying that the authenticated user owns the requested record.
Use indirect reference maps (UUIDs or cryptographic hashes) instead of direct sequential database integers.

vulnerabilities.title: [AI-Hunter] ASP.NET Diagnostic Endpoint Detected: /trace.axd
vulnerabilities.description:
### 📍 Vulnerability Location
- **Target URL / Endpoint**: `/trace.axd`
- **Full Target URL**: `http://testaspnet.vulnweb.com/trace.axd`
- **Vulnerable Parameter / Component**: N/A (Path/Header/Direct Resource)
- **Service & Port**: `http` / Port 80

### 💥 Exploitation Proof & Payload
- **Tested Payload**: `/trace.axd`
- **Verification Technique**: HTTP 403 Forbidden confirms existence of internal diagnostic module
- **CVSS v3.1 Vector**: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N`

### 🔬 Technical Analysis & Vulnerability Mechanics
Accessing http://testaspnet.vulnweb.com/trace.axd returned HTTP 403 Forbidden, confirming the module is installed on the web server. Attackers can use this information to identify ASP.NET architecture and attempt authorization bypasses.

### 📊 Threat Severity & CVSS v3.1 Scoring
- **CVSS v3.1 Base Score**: **4.3 (Low)**
- **Authoritative Classification**: **CWE-200**
- **Business Impact**: Unauthorized data compromise, application integrity degradation, or perimeter access bypass.
remediation_steps: Remove unused diagnostic handlers from web.config altogether if not required in production.

top_recommendations: Implement parameterized queries and prepared statements to eliminate SQL Injection risks.
Enforce server-side authorization checks and use indirect object references (UUID) to prevent IDOR attacks.
